Validate a complete applied household-income result

Source: R/liss_source_nonresponse_applied.R
liss_validate_applied_income.Rd

Validate the complete analytical result returned by liss_clean_income() for an explicitly selected schema-4 household s339 input in correct or na_only mode. The original native source collection is retained separately in source_input; the changed analysis frame is not a native source carrier. Whole-result RDS preserves this distinction. Extracted frames, arbitrary subsets/reorderings and column projections do not carry a complete result.

Usage

liss_validate_applied_income(result, replay = FALSE)

Arguments

result

complete applied collection result, including source_input, saved invocation and applied_lineage.

replay

one plain logical value. If TRUE, require and rerun the exact recorded computation after structural validation.

Value

invisibly, a list containing valid, validation, scoped source_readiness, analysis_execution_status and replay_status.

Details

The default structural check verifies source bindings, full row/column scope, immutable non-target columns and tax leaves, metadata, observed recovery, protected missing cells, effective configuration and receipt consistency. Constructor-owned decision, optional dataset-flag, summary and log shapes are checked, including plain count and timing types. Timing fields must have supported types before their nonsemantic values are excluded from replay. Ordinary digests are not signatures or proof that cleaning executed. An unlocked proposal and its receipts can be changed together by a caller; structural success does not establish numerical or statistical validity.

With replay = TRUE, require the recorded computation/runtime identity and rerun the saved invocation through the collection consumer. Compare complete semantic output against that execution, excluding only duration, log timestamps and ruleset source paths. Replay does not read original source files, install dependencies, export output or fit a different default method. It relies on the current trusted package/runtime and retained source evidence; it does not authenticate caller-controlled code or fabricated source receipts. If that exact computation is unavailable, structural validation may still be supported, but replay fails explicitly. Guarded reports, panels, exports, repeated consumption, background attachment and taxable cleaning are unsupported. Removing all lineage claims deliberately leaves ordinary unguarded input; names or values alone cannot recover source ownership.

Serialized object hashes use profile 1.0.0: SHA-256 over XDR version-2 R serialization with only the writer-version header fixed to R 4.6.1. All payload bytes remain significant; raw file hashes are unchanged. Compatibility covers the R 4.6.1 reference profile, not arbitrary historical writers or future serialization bodies. Other legacy profiles require their original package/runtime. Reference identity checks remain separate from digests.

New computation identities use schema 2.0.0 and record this profile. Reference-profile schema-1 records remain structurally readable, but a changed computation identity rejects replay even when the R runtime is unchanged.
